producer_report.summary: The checks step now pushes the candidate commit and reuses CI's result for it. The cause was the `NoCi` stub plus the missing push; I replaced both. After the candidate commit is made, `run_pushed` in routing.rs pushes it to `athena/<job>`. The push goes through the new `gh::push_work_branch`, which reads the remote head, calls `check_push`, then uses the existing `GitRemote::push`. `run_pushed` then waits for the `ci` run on that exact SHA through `GhClient`, up to the named constant `CI_WAIT` (60 reads, 20 seconds apart, about 20 minutes). That bound is a conservative guess and not measured, and the doc comment says so. It hands the result to `run_routed`. A green run replaces the local checks and the records name the CI run address. A red run fails and nothing runs locally. A missing or other-SHA run, or a push that cannot be made (no `origin`, no credentials, refused by the guard), runs the three checks locally once. The run output says whether the checks came from CI or ran locally. `build` jobs and capabilities without all three checks push nothing, and nested runs still skip checks. The design doc (section 10, items 4 and 5) and CHANGELOG are updated, and the verifier's reuse is still listed as not done. I added no `athena.toml` field. `cargo test --locked`, clippy and fmt all pass. The `GhClient`/`GhCli` wiring in run.rs has not been run against a real remote; the tests use fake push and CI sources. One real concern is listed under open_issues: `athena land --pr` may refuse to push once the candidate is on the work branch."

open_issues: Possible conflict with `athena land --pr`: the candidate now sits on `origin/athena/<job>`. Landing builds its own commit and, for a job with no stored PR link, runs `check_push` with the remote head set to the candidate. If the landed commit does not descend from the candidate, the guard refuses with NotFastForward. I did not change landing (out of scope), and I could not test this against a real remote. Suggested fix: let landing replace the work branch's head when the remote head is the job's own earlier candidate, or push the candidate under a separate CI-only ref.
The 20-minute CI_WAIT is not measured. If CI never triggers on the pushed branch, each job waits the full bound before running locally. Revise it once the section 9 baseline exists.
The push and CI read in run.rs use `GhCli` with the `origin` remote. I did not run them against a real remote; unit tests use fake push and CI sources.
mistakes: I did not touch ci_result.rs or athena.toml, though both are listed as deliverables. The reading needed no change in them: the wait is a constant, so no config field was added.
learnings: The candidate commit is built in `self.git` by `commit_tree` in run.rs, so it can be pushed from there.
`resolve` treats a CI source error as Missing straight away, so a failing `gh` call falls back to local without waiting out the bound.
The crate denies missing Debug impls under clippy, so `Platform` needed a manual Debug.
`JobId::parse("bootstrap")` is the idiom for job ids in tests.
desires: Read access to the saved test output. The harness stored it outside the working directory, and the read hook blocked it, so I reran with --quiet.
